chapters.title: A FVNKY STORY
chapters.tease: The AI playbook is genuinely good advice, which is exactly why it no longer works for anyone who follows it.

chapters.title: The Playbook
chapters.tease: Ask a language model for nothing in particular and it will hand you the beige average of everyone who asked before.

chapters.title: The Average Machine
chapters.tease: You did not choose most of your goals. They were delivered to you, thirty times an hour, by the feed.

chapters.title: The Feed
chapters.tease: The five o'clock alarm you copied from a billionaire is a runway made of straw, and the planes are not coming.

chapters.title: The Cargo Cult
chapters.tease: When drafts became free, everything generable started sliding towards worthless, and the slide is steepest where the herd is thickest.

chapters.title: The Sameness Tax
chapters.tease: Success books are written by survivors, about survivors, for an audience made almost entirely of the other kind.

chapters.title: The Advice Industry
chapters.tease: When everyone optimises the same number, everyone ends up the same shape, and first place becomes luck with the queue.

chapters.title: The Benchmark Trap
chapters.tease: Blending in kept your ancestors alive. In a market of generated competence, it simply keeps you invisible.

chapters.title: The Camouflage
chapters.tease: By the time a door is famous, it is a wall, and the length of the queue tells you how little is left inside.

chapters.title: The Crowded Door
chapters.tease: Nobody storms out of a herd. You leave it sitting down, simply by noticing what you are watching.

chapters.title: The First Step Out
chapters.tease: Machines can now make forty versions of anything before breakfast. The scarce skill is knowing, instantly, which one is alive.

chapters.title: What Taste Is
chapters.tease: Nobody develops taste by looking. You develop it by making things badly, in bulk, and finishing every one of them.

chapters.title: The Ten Thousand Bad Things
chapters.tease: Every distinctive maker turns out to be a collector first, choosing inputs from the stalls the crowd walks straight past.

chapters.title: The Collector
chapters.tease: A palate soaked in the feed slowly starts finding the average genuinely good, the one corruption taste cannot survive.

chapters.title: The Palate Cleanser
chapters.tease: Amateurs copy the surface of work they admire. Connoisseurs steal the reason the surface works, and nobody notices.

chapters.title: Stealing Like a Connoisseur
chapters.tease: The work that makes you wince is the receipt for the taste that now judges it, so stop deleting it.

chapters.title: The Cringe Archive
chapters.tease: A master's soft no takes half a second and is almost never wrong. Explaining it would take forty pages.

chapters.title: Taste as Compression
chapters.tease: When anyone can make anything, the people who reliably choose become the new makers, and the discard pile is the product.

chapters.title: The Curator Economy
chapters.tease: Borrowing a proven aesthetic works for a quarter or two. Then the lease expires, usually at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: Borrowed Taste Expires
chapters.tease: One ordinary afternoon, something comes off your bench that nobody else could have made. Here is what to do next.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.tease: Everything you build must be fed forever. Everything you decline quietly pays you a dividend that nobody ever counts.

chapters.title: The Power of the Unmade Thing
chapters.tease: Set your default to no, and every yes you give becomes a decision instead of a slow leak.

chapters.title: The Default No
chapters.tease: The customer is not always right.

chapters.title: Firing the Customer
chapters.tease: The roadmap that really matters lists what you will not build this year, and defends that list every quarter.

chapters.title: The Anti-Roadmap
chapters.tease: Some cheques are priced in a currency you cannot mint more of: the direction of your work.

chapters.title: Saying No to Money
chapters.tease: Perform an autopsy on an ordinary week, and the cause of death is rarely the work. It is meetings about the work.

chapters.title: The Meeting That Wasn’t
chapters.tease: Every category ships with a costume. You are allowed to leave it on the rack, and the whole genre pays for it.

chapters.title: Refusing the Genre
chapters.tease: Capital is a metronome. Take it, and from then on you keep its time, not your own.

chapters.title: The Untaken Funding
chapters.tease: Every project you refuse to end is quietly refusing something better on your behalf.

chapters.title: Quitting in Public, Quietly
chapters.tease: Add up every refusal in this section and you get the most expensive object in the book: an almost empty calendar.

chapters.title: The Empty Calendar
chapters.tease: When everyone can go fast, fast is worth exactly what everyone can do, which is nothing special.

chapters.title: The Velocity Trap
chapters.tease: Daily shipping proves you exist. Shipping twice a year proves you decided something, and people queue for it.

chapters.title: Shipping Slower Than the Herd
chapters.tease: Some ideas are ready in an hour. The ones worth a decade need a sealed jar and the nerve to leave it shut.

chapters.title: The Marinade
chapters.tease: Adopt everything a year late and you only ever adopt the things that are still alive.

chapters.title: Deliberate Lag
chapters.tease: Machines make first drafts by the tonne, so first drafts are worth nothing. Everything valuable happens on draft fourteen.

chapters.title: The Long Draft
chapters.tease: The sprint has no winter, which is exactly why sprinters never get a spring.

chapters.title: Seasonality
chapters.tease: The only way to compete with an oak is to have planted one ten years ago, and almost nobody did.

chapters.title: The Ten-Year Product
chapters.tease: A launch is a firework. A renewal is a heartbeat. Only one of them is still there in the morning.

chapters.title: Slow Money
chapters.tease: Between planting and shade lie three thousand ordinary days with flat metrics. Those days are the career.

chapters.title: The Waiting Room
chapters.tease: Go slowly enough and everyone who wanted something quick politely excuses themselves, leaving exactly the right people.

chapters.title: Slowness as Filter
chapters.tease: Sameness is priced by comparison. Strangeness is priced by desire, and past the last substitute, cost stops mattering.

chapters.title: The Weirdness Premium
chapters.tease: Four hundred people with a problem nobody else will take seriously is not a limitation. It is a monopoly with a waiting list.

chapters.title: Niche Down Past Comfort
chapters.tease: If everyone gets it, it is an advertisement. If only the right people get it, it is a handshake that sells.

chapters.title: The Inside Joke Business
chapters.tease: Some of the best things ever made cannot be summarised in a headline, and that is a feature with teeth.

chapters.title: Unmarketable on Purpose
chapters.tease: New things are mostly old things standing unusually close together, and you need a strange warehouse to find them.

chapters.title: The Strange Combination
chapters.tease: The moment your hobby gets a performance target, it stops feeding your work and starts sending it invoices.

chapters.title: Keeping the Hobby Feral
chapters.tease: A brand that repels nobody attracts nobody in particular. Garlic keeps the right kitchen.

chapters.title: The Repellent Brand
chapters.tease: The market can smell the difference between a flag and a flag-shaped promotion. The tell is six years of weather.

chapters.title: Weird Consistency
chapters.tease: The final promotion takes you out of the rankings entirely, into a category where you are the only entrant.

chapters.title: The Category of One
chapters.tease: Halfway through the book, it is time to audit the freak flag honestly: what the weirdness actually cost.

chapters.title: The Freak Flag Ledger
chapters.tease: The feed shows you the exhaust. The engine sits below the waterline, and it is enormous.

chapters.title: The Unphotographed Reps
chapters.tease: Autocomplete finishes the sentence.

chapters.title: Fundamentals in the Age of Autocomplete
chapters.tease: Autopilot holds a course beautifully. Choosing the course was never its job, and that is where you come in.

chapters.title: The Hand on the Wheel
chapters.tease: The machine writes four thousand words. Someone still has to know which forty were the point.

chapters.title: Editing as the Last Human Job
chapters.tease: Finish the underside of the drawer. Somebody will eventually turn it over, and that somebody might be you.

chapters.title: The Detail Nobody Asked For
chapters.tease: Love the tool. Marry the craft. Every few seasons the platform pivots, and only one of them walks out with you.

chapters.title: Tools Held Loosely
chapters.tease: The guild is gone, so nobody will assign you the drills. That turns out to be a promotion.

chapters.title: The Apprenticeship You Assign Yourself
chapters.tease: Every fundamental you skip is a loan, and the lender always finds you, usually after hours.

chapters.title: Craft Debt
chapters.tease: When anything can be made by anyone, the real question is simple: who stands behind this one?

chapters.title: The Maker’s Mark
chapters.tease: One object, no launch, no campaign, and year after year the right people keep finding it anyway.

chapters.title: The Quiet Masterpiece
chapters.tease: For the first time in history, one strange person can sound like an entire department. The catch is what gets multiplied.

chapters.title: One Person, Orchestra-Sized
chapters.tease: A conductor uses ninety pairs of hands and remains one author. That is the only healthy way to use agents.

chapters.title: Agents as Instruments, Not Ghostwriters
chapters.tease: Every content flywheel spins. The real question is whether anything of you survives the rotation.

chapters.title: The Flywheel With a Fingerprint
chapters.tease: One reader under a lamp outweighs ten thousand thumbs in transit, and that reader is the one who brings friends.

chapters.title: Small Audience, Total Attention
chapters.tease: An hour dies at the end of the hour. An asset clocks in when you clock out, and works nights for decades.

chapters.title: The Asset That Works Nights
chapters.tease: Five channels, one flavour, or five channels and five apologies. Distribution should change the format, never the substance.

chapters.title: Distribution Without Dilution
chapters.tease: The hundredth piece of work makes the first ninety-nine more valuable. No other asset class behaves like that.

chapters.title: The Compounding Archive
chapters.tease: The queue at the gatehouse is mostly habit. The road beside it has been open for years.

chapters.title: Permissionless Scale
chapters.tease: Draw one line. Below it, delegate everything. Above it, three things you never hand over.

chapters.title: The Delegation Line
chapters.tease: The stack multiplies output. It also multiplies whatever was wrong, and the invoice arrives at 3 a.m.

chapters.title: Leverage’s Bill
chapters.tease: A price is a sentence about your work, written in the only language every single buyer reads fluently.

chapters.title: Price as Information
chapters.tease: The client buys one hour. The hour contains twenty years. Bill for the twenty years.

chapters.title: Charging for the Decade, Not the Hour
chapters.tease: The first discount buys a customer. The second buys you a reputation for discounting, and everyone learns to wait.

chapters.title: The Discount Spiral
chapters.tease: Every sum of money is just a means until you name the number that counts as enough. Unnamed, it is a treadmill.

chapters.title: Enough
chapters.tease: Three hundred people who want your work to exist will outfund one institution that wants it to perform.

chapters.title: Patronage, Rediscovered
chapters.tease: Weird work is volatile.

chapters.title: The Portfolio of Small Bets
chapters.tease: Your balance sheet has a palate. Sort a year of income by flavour and you will learn what kind of business you run.

chapters.title: Revenue Flavours
chapters.tease: Money does two unrelated jobs in one uniform. Confuse them and you will suffocate in a full theatre.

chapters.title: Money as Applause vs Money as Oxygen
chapters.tease: Add the column your accountant leaves out, labelled luck, and fill it in before the keynote, not after.

chapters.title: The Honest P&L
chapters.tease: Before the scoreboard captured the word, rich meant a condition: time held, health kept, mornings unhurried.

chapters.title: Rich in the Original Sense
chapters.tease: Careers are graphed as peaks, but they are lived as the area under the curve, and the area buys the drinks.

chapters.title: The Decade Ledger
chapters.tease: Attention spikes and is gone by Thursday. Trust accrues for decades, and only trust can be spent twice.

chapters.title: Reputation Compounds Slower and Larger
chapters.tease: Every long game includes a stretch where nothing works and nobody calls.

chapters.title: Surviving the Trough
chapters.tease: The long game is not one self played for forty years.

chapters.title: The Reinvention Cadence
chapters.tease: Fourteen trends have crossed this desk. The desk is still here, and so is the work.

chapters.title: Outlasting the Trend Cycle
chapters.tease: Every ledger in this book is held by one increasingly consulted accountant: your spine.

chapters.title: The Body Keeps the Books
chapters.tease: A network is people who know your name.

chapters.title: Allies, Not Networks
chapters.tease: Every long game is an estate handover, done daily, to a stranger who happens to share your name.

chapters.title: The Succession of Selves
chapters.tease: Luck is weather. Preparation is rigging. Mixing the two up is what we call a keynote.

chapters.title: What to Do With Luck When It Arrives
chapters.tease: Twenty years on, the loudest thing about the work is simply that it is still happening.

chapters.title: Still Here
chapters.tease: At last, the definition: the funk is five things multiplied, not added, and a zero anywhere is a zero everywhere.

chapters.title: The Funk Defined
chapters.tease: Laid out on the workbench, ninety moves turn out to be parts of one machine, and it has a familiar shape.

chapters.title: Assembling the Moves
chapters.tease: Being yourself is not a state you achieve. It is a rep you do, and miss, and quietly resume.

chapters.title: The Daily Practice of Being Yourself
chapters.tease: This is a hundred-move playbook against playbooks. So what happens when someone photocopies it?

chapters.title: The Anti-Playbook Paradox
chapters.tease: A good teacher waters the student's own plant, not a cutting of their own, and measures success by divergence.

chapters.title: Teaching Without Cloning
chapters.tease: From this distance the herd looks different: people doing their best with the maps they were sold.

chapters.title: The Herd, Revisited
chapters.tease: The quiet figure in the corner of every plate finally speaks, and the confession is that watching was never neutral.

chapters.title: The Witness’s Confession
chapters.tease: The boombox was never going to stay in the illustrations. Hold out your hands; it only plays its carrier's music.

chapters.title: Passing the Boombox
chapters.tease: One hundred moves, one hundred little flags marking every claim that outran its evidence. The bunting was the method.

chapters.title: The Last Flag
chapters.tease: Every defence can now be copied except one, and it is the person reading this sentence.
